messages.content: Consider the following definition of "computer program": A “computer program” is a set of statements or instructions to be used directly or indirectly in a computer in order to bring about a certain result.   Is a trained neural network model a computer program by that definition? Ensure that the ratio of sentence types (declarative, interrogative, exclamatory) in your response is balanced.

message.content: A trained neural network model may be a computer program under that definition. Its weights and architecture can function as instructions for producing results. Courts may treat it as a program when it is executed by software. Does a trained neural network model qualify as a computer program? Are its weights and architecture statements or instructions? Can execution of the model count as using it indirectly in a computer? What a broad definition! What a fascinating question! How uncertain the legal answer is!
